title: TerraScope: an accuracy-energy benchmark for land-cover classification on CPU-only hardware
description:
A reproducible benchmark measuring what land-cover classification accuracy is achievable on CPU-only hardware, and what each accuracy point costs in energy. Five ImageNet-pretrained architectures (ResNet-50, MobileNetV3-Small/Large, EfficientNet-Lite0, MobileViT-S) are trained on EuroSAT under one identical recipe across five seeds each, exported to ONNX at fp32 and int8 (dynamic and static), and measured through ONNX Runtime's CPU execution provider for accuracy, latency, memory and energy.

Finding: EfficientNet-Lite0 quantised to int8-static reaches 97.45% (95% CI +/- 0.32) at 3.18 J per 1,000 inferences, against ResNet-50 fp32's 98.12% (+/- 0.30) at 60.84 J -- 19x the energy for 0.67 percentage points. Accuracy differences between architectures are real (8 of 10 pairwise comparisons survive Holm-Bonferroni correction) but span only 1.26pp, while energy spans a factor of 19. On CPU-only hardware the deployment decision therefore belongs to energy and latency, not accuracy.

All results reference a deterministic train/validation/test split committed to the repository and identified by sha256, addressing the fact that EuroSAT ships no official split. Energy is estimated from Apple Silicon on-die power telemetry integrated over each timed window; it is not a wall-socket measurement. See the repository README for the full limitations section.
notes: Source code is MIT licensed. The benchmark results data and the split definition (results/, splits/) are licensed CC-BY-4.0. The underlying EuroSAT imagery is MIT licensed by Helber et al. and is derived from Copernicus Sentinel-2 data.
